links.outcome: Critical-error rate on audiometric numerical interpretation (Q1) in case studies
links.effect: Q1 mean score 67.89 (SD 18.47) with a 35.4% (95/268) critical-error rate; errors shared across models.
links.quote: audiometric numerical interpretation (Q1) achieved a mean score of 67.89 (SD 18.47, 95% CI 65.68-70.10), with a 35.4% (95/268) critical-error rate

links.outcome: Agreement between automated adjudicator and audiologist consensus reference standard on Q1 critical errors
links.effect: Adjudicator per-item labels diverged from human judgment (kappa=0.05; sensitivity 19/26, 73%; PPV 19/53, 36%), showing automated grading alone is unreliable.
links.quote: When 2 audiologists regraded all 80 model Q1 responses with the diagnostic images available, the adjudicator's per-item Q1 labels diverged from human judgment (κ=0.05; overflagging; sensitivity: 19/26, 73%; positive predictive value: 19/53, 36%)

unlisted_practices: Human audit of LLM-as-judge adjudicator with post-stratified human-calibrated sensitivity analysis

screen.reason: The study develops and executes an automated and human-audited benchmark (AUDIOLOGYBENCH) to evaluate LLM performance in clinical audiology, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
